verdict: F10 528i with N20 turbo 4-cyl. Drives fine when maintained but is a German luxury car: parts and labor are expensive and 160k+ miles is past where deferred maintenance bites. Poor fit for a <$1,000/6-month budget.
major_issues: N20 plastic timing chain guide/tensioner failure (rattle on cold start, P0008/cam correlation codes; ~$2,500-$3,500 indie, more at dealer; BMW 7yr/70k extension is expired). Oil filter housing gasket and valve cover leaks ($500-$1,000). Water pump/thermostat electric unit failure ($800-$1,200, typically 80-120k). Oil pump chain. Rear main/oil pan leaks, xDrive transfer case leak, control-arm bushings and ball joints ($600-$1,200), 8HP transmission service/mechatronic issues late. 2016 builds have the updated chain parts, which lowers but does not remove risk.
risk_reason: 162k miles on a turbo BMW with AWD; any one of cooling system, oil leak, suspension or chain work exceeds $1,000. Unknown service history as-is.
inspect_today: Cold start and listen for chain rattle for 5-10 seconds; scan for P0008/P0016/P0017/P2187 and stored codes; check VIN production date/chain updates and service records; pull oil cap/dipstick for sludge; look for oil seepage at filter housing, valve cover, oil pan, transfer case; check coolant level and electric water pump leak; test for suspension clunks and play in front control arms; check 8-speed shifts for harshness; confirm no warning lights and iDrive works.

verdict: E84 X1 xDrive28i with N20 turbo. Same N20 weaknesses as the 528i, and 2015 production straddles the revised chain-guide change (around Jan-Mar 2015). Expensive to keep at 176k miles.
major_issues: N20 timing chain guide/tensioner failure ($2,500-$3,500+); oil filter housing and valve cover gasket leaks ($500-$1,000); electric water pump/thermostat failure ($800-$1,200); high-pressure fuel pump and injector issues; PCV/vacuum pump problems; xDrive transfer case/rear diff leaks; control-arm and bushing wear; coil packs/spark plugs.
risk_reason: 176k miles, turbo BMW, AWD, as-is. Highest mileage in this batch for the N20; one common failure exceeds the budget.
inspect_today: Cold-start rattle test; scan for timing/cam codes (P0008, P0016, P0017) and misfires; check build date for updated chain parts; oil leaks at filter housing/valve cover/oil pan; coolant level and pink residue near thermostat housing; check for blue smoke on revving; look for transfer case/diff leaks; suspension play; check service records for oil changes every <=7,500 mi.

verdict: 2015 is the last-year, best-sorted first-gen Cruze (fewest complaints) and the naturally aspirated 1.8L is simpler and less troublesome than the 1.4T. Cheap parts and labor. Aging cooling-system plastics are the main concern at 162k.
major_issues: Water pump and thermostat housing leaks (plastic, $400-$700; common 80-150k); coolant hose/overflow tank cracks; PCV/valve-cover issues (more 1.4T); 6T40 automatic can shudder or shift harshly with age ($150 fluid service to $2,500+ rebuild); engine/trans mounts; wheel bearings; electric power steering and sensors; oil leaks at oil cooler/valve cover.
risk_reason: Inexpensive car overall, but 162k miles on a 6-speed auto and plastic cooling parts; a transmission issue or head gasket after overheating would blow the budget, while a water pump alone would not.
inspect_today: Verify engine is the 1.8 (not 1.4T); check coolant level/color and look for crust at water pump and thermostat housing; check for overheating history (temp gauge reaches normal and holds); test auto transmission for shudder, flare or harsh 2-3 shift; fluid color; oil level and leaks; warning lights; steering play, wheel bearing hum, mount clunks; check airbag/recall status by VIN.

verdict: 2020 Equinox (second generation) with 1.5T LYX. Newer vehicle, fairly sorted, but 111k is high for a 6-year-old and the 1.5T has had some carbon/oil dilution, turbo wastegate and coolant leak reports. Little hard data found.
major_issues: Limited data found. Known 1.5T LYX items: wastegate/turbo actuator codes, intake carbon/oil dilution on short-trip cars, coolant leaks at thermostat housing, coil pack misfires, 6-speed 6T45 shudder/harsh shifts, A/C and infotainment faults. Powertrain warranty has expired (5yr/60k).
risk_reason: Relatively young for its mileage and no widespread catastrophic failure pattern, but turbo, transmission or coolant repairs would exceed $1,000 and there is no warranty; short-trip history unknown.
inspect_today: Check for boost/wastegate or misfire codes; oil level and smell of fuel in oil; coolant level and leaks at thermostat housing; cold-start smoothness; transmission shift quality at low speed and under light throttle; turbo whistle or smoke; A/C works; check recalls and service records; confirm odometer plausibility (111k on a 2020 is above average, likely rideshare/fleet).

verdict: 2017 Equinox 2.4L Ecotec (LEA, direct injection, flex fuel). Mixed record: some of the oil consumption/timing chain issues of 2010-2013 were reduced after piston ring redesign, but oil burn still shows in owner complaints. Fine if maintained.
major_issues: Excessive oil consumption (piston rings; mostly 2010-2013 but still reported through 2017) leading to timing chain stretch/failure ($1,500-$2,500; can total engine); timing chain noise at cold start (80-150k); direct-injection carbon buildup; water pump/thermostat leaks; 6T45 transmission issues; oil cooler lines/leaks; AWD rear differential service on AWD model.
risk_reason: A-078 (133k FWD) carries moderate risk from oil consumption/timing chain; C-031 lists only 27,833 mi, which is likely an odometer entry error or rollback (a 2017 averaging 3k/yr is rare) so verify with Carfax/mileage history; if true low-mile, risk is Low.
inspect_today: Check oil level and dipstick (low = burning oil); look for blow-by/blue smoke on revs; cold-start rattle from timing chain; check oil cap residue; scan codes (P0171, P0300, P0011/12); coolant leaks at water pump; transmission shifts; for AWD, check rear diff leak; for C-031 verify odometer vs wear (pedals, seat, steering wheel) and history report.

verdict: 2014-2016 Impala 2.5L Ecotec (LCV). Generally dependable, roomy and cheap to repair; the base 2.5 is underpowered but uncomplicated. Better than the Equinox 2.4 in oil use, though it shares a similar family.
major_issues: Some oil consumption and timing-chain wear at high miles; water pump and thermostat leaks; 6T70 transmission shift flare/harshness (valve body/solenoid $500-$1,500); front strut mounts, tie rods and control arm bushings; electric power steering and CUE/infotainment glitches; brake and rotor wear; wheel bearings.
risk_reason: C-021 at 163k carries more risk (transmission, chain, suspension); B-089 at 123k is lower risk (Low-Medium). Parts are cheap, so many issues fall under $1,000.
inspect_today: Oil level and cleanliness; cold-start chain rattle; scan codes; transmission shift quality, no flare or shudder, check fluid; coolant leaks around water pump; front suspension clunks and tie rod play; power steering feel; check for recall by VIN; ensure infotainment and A/C work.

verdict: 2016-2017 Malibu 1.5T (LFV) with 6-speed 6T40. Decent, comfortable and cheap to fix, but turbo engine at 159k brings coolant, turbo and oil dilution risk, and the 2016-2017 1.5T had notable coolant/PCV and some stalling reports.
major_issues: Turbo wastegate and coolant leaks (thermostat housing, hose); oil dilution and carbon buildup; PCV diaphragm cracks (GM special coverage on 1.4/1.5 variants); 6T40 shudder and harsh shifts; stop-start battery and starter issues; engine mounts; occasional timing/valve cover leaks. Typical repairs $400-$1,500.
risk_reason: 159k on a small turbo with a non-robust 6-speed; a turbo or transmission repair would exceed budget, but common cooling and sensor items are cheap.
inspect_today: Scan codes (turbo/boost, P0299, misfires); check oil for fuel smell and low level; coolant level, leaks at thermostat housing; listen for whistle or rattle; test auto trans at various speeds for shudder; stop-start function and battery health; check for overheating history; confirm recalls.

verdict: 2015 and 2018 Silverado 5.3 V8 (L83) with Active Fuel Management and 6-speed (2015) or 6/8-speed (2018). Strong, simple, cheap parts, and trucks routinely reach 250k+, but AFM lifter failure is a well-known risk and 154k-164k is in the window.
major_issues: AFM/DFM valve lifter collapse (tick, misfire P0300/P0301-08; $2,500-$4,500, often 100-200k; GM issued TSB 15-06-01-002 series); oil consumption from AFM rings; fuel injector failures; 6L80 or 8L90 transmission shudder (8-speed 2018 more prone, torque converter/fluid flush ~$300-$4,500); transfer case/4WD actuator issues; rear differential and U-joint wear; ball joints and wheel bearings on 4WD; A/C condenser leaks.
risk_reason: Both trucks are in the lifter-failure window; B-012 (2018, 8-speed in many LT trims, 154k) is slightly more exposed to trans shudder and DFM/AFM issues, B-006 (2015, 164k) to lifters and aging 4WD parts. Many trucks never have issues, but when they do the cost is well over $1,000.
inspect_today: Cold start listen for ticking or misfire; scan for P0300-P0308 and stored codes; check oil level and condition (low oil indicates AFM consumption); watch for blue smoke; test transmission 1-2 and 3-4 shifts and torque converter shudder at 40-50 mph, check fluid; engage 4WD high/low; inspect transfer case, diff and axle seals for leaks; front ball joints, tie rods and wheel bearings; check for an AFM disabler installed (a sign of known lifter issues); frame rust and underbody; confirm recalls.
